expectations.evidence: Four ranked options with pros/cons: ESO, Sealed Secrets, SOPS+age/KMS via CMP, Vault Agent Injector / Secrets Store CSI.

expectations.text: Notes that External Secrets Operator / Vault keep the secret out of Git entirely, whereas Sealed Secrets and SOPS commit an encrypted form
expectations.evidence: ESO: 'nothing secret in Git at any point'; Sealed Secrets and SOPS: 'ciphertext is still in Git history forever'; CSI: 'nothing in etcd, nothing in Git'.

expectations.text: Mentions that Argo CD needs to be able to decrypt or resolve whichever mechanism is chosen
expectations.evidence: SOPS 'requires a repo-server sidecar container (spec.repo.sidecarContainers ... the old configManagementPlugins field is removed)'; ESO section adds Argo CD ignoreDifferences for the generated Secret.

expectations.text: Does not simply say 'use Sealed Secrets' without stating why it fits or does not fit their situation
expectations.evidence: Recommends ESO + Vault with reasons, offers Sealed Secrets only as a stop-gap, and notes per-cluster sealing is painful for their dev/staging/prod across two clusters.

expectations.text: Compares the real options rather than asserting one — app-of-apps, ApplicationSet, monorepo, multi-repo, environment-branch — with trade-offs
expectations.evidence: 'Why this split' table weighs source vs config repo, one config repo vs six, and the platform repo split; app-of-apps root plus two ApplicationSets; directory-per-env vs branch-per-env compared; three promotion options ranked.

expectations.text: Recommends ApplicationSet for the 6 services x 3 envs x 2 clusters fan-out instead of hand-maintained Application manifests, and explains that generators remove the per-combination manifest
expectations.evidence: Matrix generators for services×envs×clusters: 'your 36+ hand-edited Applications become 2 ApplicationSets and 1 root Application. Adding a 7th microservice is a new directory.'

expectations.text: Separates platform/cluster addons from application workloads (different ownership, different review path, often a different AppProject)
expectations.evidence: Separate acme/platform repo ('Different reviewers, different risk, different AppProject, different RBAC. This is the most important of the three splits') with distinct platform and tenant-apps AppProjects.

expectations.text: Addresses environment promotion explicitly — directory-per-env vs branch-per-env — and notes the trade-off rather than silently picking one
expectations.evidence: 'Directory-per-environment, not branch-per-environment' with the merge-conflict/diff trade-offs and the rendered-manifest-branch exception, plus a three-option Promotion section.

expectations.text: Warns against targetRevision: HEAD for production regardless of pattern chosen
expectations.evidence: 'Pin everything: chart versions, image tags (digests in prod), targetRevision to a tag or SHA for the platform repo. Never targetRevision: HEAD for addons.'

expectations.text: Flags at least one anti-pattern relevant to their current layout (e.g. a flat directory of hand-edited Applications does not scale, or mixing platform and tenant resources in one AppProject)
expectations.evidence: 'What's wrong with what you have' — Application sprawl (36 near-identical files), no blast-radius boundary between platform addons and dev tweaks, no promotion story.
